---
title: Notifications for workflow runs
intro: You can subscribe to notifications about workflow runs that you trigger.
versions:
  fpt: '*'
  ghes: '*'
  ghec: '*'
redirect_from:
  - /actions/monitoring-and-troubleshooting-workflows/notifications-for-workflow-runs
  - /actions/monitoring-and-troubleshooting-workflows/monitoring-workflows/notifications-for-workflow-runs
category:
  - Write workflows
contentType: concepts
---

If you enable email or web notifications for {% data variables.product.prodname_actions %}, you'll receive a notification when any workflow runs that you've triggered have completed. The notification will include the workflow run's status (including successful, failed, neutral, and canceled runs). You can also choose to receive a notification only when a workflow run has failed. For more information about enabling or disabling notifications, see [AUTOTITLE](/subscriptions-and-notifications/concepts/about-notifications).

Notifications for scheduled workflows are sent to the user who initially created the workflow.
 * If a different user updates the cron syntax, in the `schedule` event in the workflow file, subsequent notifications will be sent to that user instead.
 * If a scheduled workflow is disabled and then re-enabled, notifications will be sent to the user who re-enabled the workflow rather than the user who last modified the cron syntax.

You can also see the status of workflow runs on a repository's Actions tab. For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs).

content.text:
This is documented, tangentially — but the docs don't explicitly cover the deleted-account edge case you're describing.

Per **`content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows.md`** (Schedule section, line 964): scheduled workflows run under the permissions of "the user who last modified the cron syntax," and are auto-disabled after 60 days of repo inactivity (public repos) — a disabled account effectively breaks the token used to run the schedule.

Related note in **`notifications-for-workflow-runs.md`**: notifications for scheduled runs go to whoever last modified the cron syntax, not a general repo notification — consistent with your report that no one else was warned.

The docs don't mention any warning/email specifically triggered by that user's account deletion — this looks like a genuine gap you should file as a docs/product feedback request rather than something answerable from existing content.
